__comment_purpose: Reads external endpoint findings from Loki after a compatible sensor exports OTLP logs to DefenseClaw's bundled local collector. The final row places DefenseClaw's AI component discoveries beside endpoint detections; each producer keeps its own service namespace.
__comment_attribution: Adapted for DefenseClaw's fixed Loki datasource from the ShadowClaw dashboard by Mike Storm. Redistributed under the ShadowClaw BSD 3-Clause License with Attribution Requirement; see SHADOWCLAW_LICENSE.md in this bundle.
title: Shadow AI Discovery Board
description: Unsanctioned AI use detected on this endpoint by correlating process compute behaviour with per-process network egress. Author: Mike Storm, Distinguished Engineer, CCIE Security 13847. Includes the host plane: credential access, identity creation, privilege escalation, persistence and exfiltration performed by local AI agents, gated on agent process lineage.

panels.title: Findings
panels.description: Total findings the endpoint sensor reported in the selected window.

panels.title: Critical
panels.description: Findings the endpoint sensor scored as critical risk.

panels.title: Providers reached
panels.description: Distinct AI providers reached in the window. Counts every provider a process talked to, not just the one that headlined its finding — a single agent reaching Anthropic and Fireworks counts as two.

panels.title: Processes implicated
panels.description: Distinct processes responsible for the findings above.

panels.title: Peak risk score
panels.description: Highest risk score reached in the window. The endpoint sensor scores 0-100; 30 is the default reporting floor.

panels.title: Sensor reporting
panels.description: Findings in the last 5 minutes. Zero means either a quiet endpoint or a sensor that is not running — check the sensor ledger to tell the two apart.

panels.title: Risk score over time, by provider
panels.description: Risk score attributed to each provider over time. One series per provider actually reached; a process talking to several contributes to all of their series, not only to the alphabetically-first one. The 'unattributed egress' series is separate because it reads findings with no provider at all, which emit no provider record.

targets.expr: max by (provider) (max_over_time({service_name="shadowclaw"} | shadowclaw_event_name="shadowclaw.provider.reached" | json | __error__="" | severity =~ "$severity" |~ "$search" | unwrap risk_score [$__interval]) by (provider))

panels.title: Providers by finding count
panels.description: Which providers this host reaches most. Counts per provider reached rather than per headline provider, so a second provider on the same process is visible instead of being hidden behind the first.

panels.title: Findings by severity
panels.description: Detection rate split by severity, to separate a steady low-grade background from a genuine escalation.

panels.title: Endpoint findings
panels.description: The findings themselves. Expand a line to see every field: process identity, the endpoint reached, the signals that fired, and the attribution confidence behind the provider name.

panels.title: Side by side with DefenseClaw AI Discovery
DefenseClaw — AI discovery scans
panels.description: DefenseClaw's own continuous AI-discovery scans, read-only, for correlation. One line per completed scan with its source and the new / changed / gone signal counts. Discovery establishes what AI is present on this host; it does not claim any of it is active -- which is the question the endpoint-observation rows above answer.

panels.title: DefenseClaw — security findings
panels.description: DefenseClaw's own security findings, read-only, for correlation. Expect volume from the AIBOM scanner: rule ids under aibom-claw.* are INFO-level inventory enumerations -- 'Tools (0)' against a connector config -- rather than security conclusions, and there is one per config file per category. Filter them out with | body_defenseclaw_finding_rule_id !~ "aibom-claw.*" if this panel is only ever read for real findings.

panels.title: Host plane — what the agent did to the machine
panels.description: Requires the sensor to run with Endpoint Security enabled (root, and Full Disk Access on some builds). These panels are empty rather than broken on an unprivileged sensor — except agent-config persistence, which needs no privilege.

panels.title: Kill chains
panels.description: Agents that progressed through three or more attack stages in order. This is the number to page on: a single tactic is a lead, a chain is an incident.

panels.title: Credentials read
panels.description: Distinct secrets at rest opened by an agent or one of its descendants. Once a chain fires, this is the rotation list.

panels.title: Identities created
panels.description: Local accounts, group memberships and cloud IAM principals minted by an agent. The step that converts a transient foothold into durable access.

panels.title: Persistence
panels.description: Launch items, profiles and shell rc files written by an agent, plus agent-config persistence: an agent rewriting its own standing instructions so it survives into every future session.

panels.title: Exfil surfaces
panels.description: Reaches to anonymous paste sites, file drops, webhook relays and tunnels. Modern exfiltration needs no attacker infrastructure and goes to a domain most egress policies already allow.

panels.title: Tactics observed
panels.description:
Total attributed observations, which is the denominator for everything else in this row.

A zero here is ambiguous and deliberately not dressed up as reassurance: it means either nothing happened, or Endpoint Security is not running and nothing could be seen. This datasource is Loki and cannot answer which. Check the shadowclaw.esf.running metric, or the sensor's startup banner, before reading a zero as clean.

panels.title: Tactics over time, by stage
panels.description: The shape of an incident. Isolated bars are ordinary agent work; a staircase climbing from credential access through to exfiltration is a chain in progress.

panels.title: Agents by tactic count
panels.description: Which agent is doing the most to this host. Names come from process lineage, so a tactic performed by a shell three levels below the agent is still attributed to the agent.

panels.title: Agent activity timeline
panels.description: Every attributed tactic in order — the timeline an analyst reconstructs an incident from. Expand a line for the ATT&CK technique, the confidence, and the file or endpoint involved.

panels.title: Kinetic Trust Protocol — conditions, and how much of them we could see
Inputs unobserved
panels.description: How many of the four Risk Factors are reporting a maximum-stress substitute rather than a measurement. Read this before reading any factor: an unobserved input is 1.0 by rule, so a high factor beside a non-zero count here is blindness, not hostility.

panels.title: Feed coverage
panels.description: Share of the eleven declared feeds that reported this poll. Below 100% some factor is partly substituted. An unprivileged sensor sits at 73% and cannot go higher — that is the Plane C gap, not a fault.

panels.title: Adversarial pressure
panels.description: Hostility in what the sensor can see: kill-chain progression, escalating findings, tactic volume. Floors at 0.714 without root and Full Disk Access, because three of its seven feeds are Plane C. Shows the last *measured* value only — polls where this input was unobserved are excluded, so the panel reads "unobserved" rather than showing the 1.0 substitute as if it were a reading.

panels.title: Evidence density
panels.description: How crowded the picture is: candidate runtimes, distinct egress peers, total connections. Congestion, not evidentiary weight. Shows the last *measured* value only — polls where this input was unobserved are excluded, so the panel reads "unobserved" rather than showing the 1.0 substitute as if it were a reading.

panels.title: Trust trend
panels.description: Direction of travel across polls. 0.5 is the no-prior-poll neutral, above it means conditions are worsening. Shows the last *measured* value only — polls where this input was unobserved are excluded, so the panel reads "unobserved" rather than showing the 1.0 substitute as if it were a reading.

panels.title: Update resistance
panels.description: How settled the standing is: observation time, heartbeat streaks, egress samples. Low means the picture could still move a lot. Shows the last *measured* value only — polls where this input was unobserved are excluded, so the panel reads "unobserved" rather than showing the 1.0 substitute as if it were a reading.

panels.title: Risk Factors over time
panels.description: All four stress terms, every poll, on a 0-1 scale where 1 is maximum stress. Substituted values are drawn rather than dropped, because a line that vanishes when the sensor goes dark is indistinguishable from a line that fell to calm. Read this panel against the one to its right: a step up here that coincides with a fall in coverage there is the sensor losing sight, not the host getting worse.

panels.title: Could we see it?
panels.description: The confidence behind the numbers on the left. Coverage is the share of declared feeds that reported; unobserved inputs is how many factors were substituted outright. Silent processes are tracked processes whose window held no readings — kept on the chart rather than reaped, so a process that went quiet stays distinguishable from one reporting calm.

panels.title: Risk Factor snapshots
panels.description: One line per poll, emitted whether or not anything happened — a factor is only interpretable against the polls around it. The summary names any input that was substituted. Expand a line for per-input feed counts and the KTP spec version the values were produced under.

targets.expr: {service_name="shadowclaw"} | shadowclaw_event_name="shadowclaw.ktp.risk_factors" | json | __error__="" |~ "$search" | line_format "cover {{.feed_coverage}} | AP {{.adversarial_pressure}} ED {{.evidence_density}} TT {{.trust_trend}} UR {{.update_resistance}} | {{.summary}}"

panels.title: Deduplication — what DefenseClaw already accounts for
Corroboration unavailable
panels.description: Findings where DefenseClaw's inventory could not be relied on -- absent, stale, or unparseable. Read this first. These findings were neither attenuated nor escalated, so the two panels to the right are silent about them rather than clearing them. A high number here means the endpoint sensor is scoring alone, not that the host is quiet.

panels.title: Already inventoried
panels.description: Findings DefenseClaw independently accounts for: a local model artifact it has on disk, or an MCP server declared in an agent configuration it scanned. These were attenuated, and the ones with nothing else behind them fell below the reporting floor entirely. This is the noise the integration removes.

panels.title: Not accounted for
panels.description: Findings a *fresh* DefenseClaw inventory did not explain. This is the disagreement, and it is the more interesting reading: their model_file detector walks the filesystem, so sustained local inference with no inventoried artifact means the weights are not somewhere a scanner can see them.

panels.title: DefenseClaw accounts for these
panels.description: Corroborated findings, at their attenuated scores. Worth a glance rather than an investigation -- the governance tool on this host already knows about the subject.

panels.title: DefenseClaw has never seen these
panels.description: The queue to actually work. Local AI that the endpoint sensor observed running and a current DefenseClaw scan cannot explain.
